attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, endorsed. He is not quoting anyone else.

semantics.note: The firm part is a present-tense observation about Chinese law. The hedges on Putin ('probably') and the US ('not inconceivable... might') are kept as qualifiers and are not scored. Paraphrasing 'on it' as 'doing the same' is acceptable.

contract.note: Reading 'Party line' as the 'core socialist values' in binding AI rules is a fair, ordinary plain reading, given the LLM context. A broader reading of Chinese law would give the same result, so the interpretation does not decide it.

evidence.note: Official CAC text of the Interim Measures. Article 4 is mandatory ('shall'), and the measures took effect 2023-08-15, inside the target window.
A law firm's English translation of Article 4(1), matching the CAC text. It requires adherence to core socialist values and bans subversion of the socialist system.
July 2024 CNBC/FT report that the CAC tests LLMs for core socialist values. Under the contract, reporting on enforcement is context; it does indicate the rule was still in force.

reviews.rationale: Binding CAC rules in force from August 2023 require generative AI services to adhere to core socialist values and ban content against the socialist system. Nothing in the packet suggests they were withdrawn before June 2025, and 2024 reporting shows they were enforced. The firm China claim is supported. The Putin and US parts are hedged and not scored.
